analysis.summary: Open circular pocket compass with hinged brass-toned lid resting on rough rock, showing a graduated bezel, decorative compass rose, and central magnetic needle under a transparent cover.

components.name: Hinged Lid / Protective Cover
components.function: Covers and protects the compass face when closed; shown open away from dial
components.evidence: Large circular gold-toned disc above dial with concentric brushed finish and strong specular highlight, open about 90 degrees

components.name: Outer Case / Housing
components.function: Encloses and supports the dial and bezel; provides structural body
components.evidence: Gold-toned circular body around dial sitting on textured gray rock with visible side thickness and shadow

components.name: Rotating Bezel with Degree Scale
components.function: Provides 0-360 degree markings for orienting and reading bearings relative to north
components.evidence: White outer ring encircling dial with black numerals 20,40,60 to 340 and red N at top edge

components.name: Compass Dial / Compass Rose
components.function: Displays cardinal and intercardinal directions as reference for needle indication
components.evidence: Inner face with printed N, E, S, W, degree ticks and brown concentric pattern visible through clear cover
material_candidates: printed card or dial under transparent cover
possible glass or clear plastic cover

components.name: Magnetic Needle Assembly on Central Pivot
components.function: Aligns with Earth's magnetic field to indicate magnetic north-south
components.evidence: Ornate dark pointer with red-accented north end pivoted at central silver pin, casting small shadow on dial

components.name: Suspension Loop / Bail
components.function: Allows attachment of lanyard, chain, or clip for carrying
components.evidence: Small gold-toned loop with circular ring protruding from bottom of case resting on rock

principles.name: Magnetic Alignment
principles.explanation: Needle is inferred to be magnetized to align with Earth's magnetic field, with one end indicating toward magnetic north. Visible red/N marking corresponds to that end.

principles.name: Low-Friction Pivot Suspension
principles.explanation: Central pin allows needle to rotate freely so it can settle toward magnetic north with minimal friction. The needle's balanced appearance suggests it is supported at center.

principles.name: Azimuth Reference via Graduated Bezel
principles.explanation: Outer numbered ring provides angular reference around the dial. User likely rotates bezel or case to compare needle direction to markings, but rotation mechanism is not visibly in motion here.

uncertainty: Exact materials, plating, or presence of glass versus plastic cannot be determined from photo alone
Dimensions, weight, and manufacturing date or maker are not visible
Whether compass is fluid-damped, dry, or includes declination adjustment is not discernible
Magnetic accuracy, calibration, and current functional state cannot be verified from single still image
Internal construction under dial such as pivot jewel type or magnet attachment is hidden
Geographic location, true north vs magnetic north offset, and local magnetic interference are unknown
next_steps: Photograph underside and side hinge to show closing mechanism and any maker marks
Take close-up straight-down photo of dial markings to read scale increments more clearly
Observe needle movement briefly in a video to confirm free rotation, without disassembly
safety_notes: Do not rely on a decorative or uncalibrated compass for critical navigation; verify against known reference
Keep away from magnets, speakers, phones, and large metal masses that can deflect or demagnetize needle
Do not open, disassemble, or attempt to modify sealed housing; no wiring or hazardous procedures are involved
Image-based assessment cannot confirm accuracy or condition
